soundness_flags.label: ass:sparse-graph
soundness_flags.one_line: The cited source formulates sparse interference as directed, unit-specific neighborhoods with arbitrary response functions, not the stated undirected symmetric maximum-degree graph condition; replace the citation with one supporting this exact condition or retag it novel.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper permits assignments with ℓ1 norm at most B, uses singleton isolation in its ETC phase, proves the displayed O(n² log(nT)) discovery upper bound in Theorem 2, and gives a B=1 disjoint-pair Ω(n log T) lower bound in Theorem 3.

source_verification_receipts.locator: p. 4, Assumption 2 and graphical interpretation, extracted lines 294–335
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper assumes a unit-specific neighborhood N(n) of size at most s, permits arbitrary dependence on that neighborhood, and explicitly interprets the graph as directed; it does not state an undirected symmetric maximum-degree graph assumption.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 1–2, introduction and Table 1, extracted lines 31–45 and 51–69
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies sparse linear bandits with an exploration-distribution eigenvalue condition and information-regret tradeoffs, rather than network recovery under constant-weight actions.
